item.title: Ammonia-Hydrogen Phase Equilibria in Planetary Envelopes from First-Principles-Based Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.27136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ammonia and hydrogen are major constituents of planets within and beyond the solar system, yet how they interact in planetary envelopes is poorly known. We perform large-scale two-phase coexistence simulations of the ammonia-hydrogen system from 500 to 4000 K and 0.1 to 100 GPa, driven by machine-learning interatomic potentials trained on density functional theory calculations. From these we map the compositions of coexisting hydrogen-rich and ammonia-rich phases, and the critical curve that separates conditions of complete miscibility from those of phase separation. The critical temperature increases with pressure, from 500 K at 0.1 GPa to 2000 K near 30 GPa, and we find no phase separation at 3000 and 4000 K up to 100 GPa. The slope of the critical curve decreases substantially between 0.3 and 30 GPa, and the curve nearly flattens above about 30 GPa and 2000 K, where molecules begin to give way to atomic species. The coexistence curves are asymmetric with an ammonia-rich critical composition. For the expected envelope compositions, the phase boundary lies close to, and intersects, published thermal profiles of Uranus and Neptune, implying ammonia may be raining out in these planets today. In contrast, in warm sub-Neptunes such as TOI-270 d, ammonia and hydrogen are likely miscible in all proportions. Together with previous studies, our results suggest that silicates, water and ammonia separate from hydrogen in sequence as planets cool, with implications for their compositional, thermal and structural evolution.
item.dc:creator: Akash Gupta, Austin Guo, Jie Deng

item.title: Counterexamples to the total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.27294v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture asserts that the ground-state particle density and total current determine the scalar potential up to an additive constant and the vector potential up to a gauge transformation. We give three counterexamples for two spinless fermions in the physically relevant setting of three spatial dimensions. In each, a Hamiltonian $H^{v,\mathbf{A}}$ has a nondegenerate ground state with identically zero total current but nonzero magnetic field. Complex conjugation then yields a second Hamiltonian $H^{v,-\mathbf{A}}$, with the same scalar potential and interaction, whose ground state has the same density and the same zero current, while the magnetic field is reversed. The first two examples are noninteracting. One is explicit, with a smooth bounded vector potential and a Gaussian density. The other has smooth bounded scalar and vector potentials in the standard potential spaces. The third example has Coulomb repulsion with unit coupling, an isotropic harmonic scalar potential, and Dirac monopole fields of magnetic charge $\pm 1/2$. The monopole example uses vector potentials defined on separate spatial patches, since these fields are not curls of globally defined smooth vector potentials.
item.dc:creator: Andre Laestadius, Mih\'aly A. Csirik

item.title: Effect of interfacial water structure on the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions
item.description: arXiv:2610.27964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weakly hydrated anions tend to partition to macromolecular surfaces, leading to salting-in at low salt concentrations. Recent studies have linked this partitioning to disruption of the interfacial water network. Here, we investigate the role of interfacial-water-network disruption as an indirect driving force for the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions and its interplay with direct solute-anion and anion-cation interactions using computer simulations. We study the adsorption of SCN$^{-}$ and I$^{-}$ ions on a model extended solute that interacts with water and ions only via van der Waals interactions. To probe the indirect contribution, we increase the effective solute size while simultaneously decreasing the attractive solute-water and solute-ion interactions, resulting in progressively greater disorder in the interfacial water network in pure aqueous solutions. Our results show that iodide adsorption increases despite weaker direct solute-iodide interactions and correlates with greater disruption of the interfacial water network, although iodide remains depleted overall. In contrast, preferential adsorption of SCN$^{-}$ decreases, but the rate of decrease becomes smaller at higher levels of interfacial-water-network disorder. This suggests that the indirect contribution associated with interfacial-water-network disruption partly compensates for the decrease in SCN$^{-}$ adsorption caused by weaker direct solute-SCN$^{-}$ interactions. Our results highlight that the indirect contribution associated with interfacial-water-network disruption promotes the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions on macromolecular surfaces, while the extent of adsorption also depends on direct solute-ion interactions and anion-cation pairing. This interplay may be particularly important in mixed-salt solutions, where the presence of strongly hydrated anions can also disrupt the interfacial water network.
item.dc:creator: Swaminath Bharadwaj

item.title: Gel-Chemistry-Controlled Heavy-Metal Transport and Retention in Cementitious Gel Nanopores: A Molecular Dynamics Study
item.description: arXiv:2605.11604v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cementitious materials are widely used for hazardous-waste encapsulation, yet molecular mechanisms governing heavy-metal ion retention across gel chemistries remain insufficiently resolved. Previous MD studies have focused on individual gel systems and pore-averaged metrics, limiting direct comparison across gel chemistries. Here, classical molecular dynamics simulations were used to investigate adsorption-controlled mobility of Pb2+, Ba2+, and Cs+ in nanopores of C-S-H, C-(N)-A-S-H, and N-A-S-H gels. Combining pore-averaged and spatially resolved diffusivity, residence-time analysis, ion-density profiles, 2D adsorption maps, radial distribution functions, coordination analysis, and interfacial binding-strength descriptors establishes a framework linking gel surface chemistry to mobility suppression while distinguishing local mobility from spatial ion partitioning effects on pore-averaged transport. Ion mobility is reduced in all gel nanopores relative to bulk, but the extent and mechanism vary strongly with gel chemistry. C-(N)-A-S-H with higher interfacial Al/Si substitution exhibits the strongest retention, driven by ion accumulation around Al-linked oxygen species via an ion-exchange-like mechanism with charge-balancing Na+. C-S-H immobilizes ions primarily through surface hydroxyl oxygens and Ca-mediated linkages, whereas N-A-S-H exhibits more distributed binding environments. Pb2+ and Ba2+ show broadly similar immobilization mechanisms, whereas Cs+ exhibits more gel-dependent interactions with silicate and aluminosilicate oxygen sites. A relative total binding strength (rTBS) descriptor shows a strong positive correlation with ion immobilization across gel types, ion species, and pore sizes. These results clarify gel- and ion-specific retention mechanisms and link interfacial binding strength to pore-averaged mobility suppression in idealized cementitious nanopores.

item.title: Excited-state Properties Beyond the Excitation Energy from Orbital-Optimized Density Functional Calculations I: Dipole Moments of Rydberg States
item.description: arXiv:2606.12272v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rydberg excited states are challenging to describe due to their highly diffuse character. Orbital-optimized density functional calculations typically provide more accurate values of the excitation energy of Rydberg states than time-dependent density functional theory approaches, but their performance with respect to excited-state properties such as the dipole moment remains largely unexplored as existing benchmarks are limited to the lowest excited state. Here, orbital-optimized density functional calculations with a plane-wave basis set are used to compute the dipole moment of several Rydberg states of a set of small molecules. Plane waves provide a flexible representation of diffuse Rydberg orbitals, whereas commonly used atomic orbitals basis sets are found to yield significant discrepancies in the magnitude and orientation of the dipole moment, even when diffuse functions are included and the excitation energy agrees well with the plane-wave results. The generalized gradient approximation functional PBE used in combination with the plane-wave representation of the orbitals gives good agreement with higher-level coupled-cluster calculations performed with sufficiently diffuse basis sets, when the latter are available. The hybrid functional PBE0 further improves the results, while PBE with globally scaled explicit Perdew-Zunger self-interaction correction generally leads to larger errors and an overestimation of the dipole moment, despite restoring the correct asymptotic $-1/r$ dependence of the effective Kohn--Sham potential.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Restaino, Jukka John, Diego Llorena Prieto, Yorick Leonard Adrian Schmerwitz, Elvar \"Orn J\'onsson, Gianluca Levi

item.title: Excited-state Properties Beyond the Excitation Energy from Orbital-Optimized Density Functional Calculations II: Absorption Spectra
item.description: arXiv:2606.13243v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Previous benchmarks of orbital-optimized density functional calculations of transition intensities in molecules have primarily been restricted to the lowest electronic excitation. Here, the performance of this variational approach is assessed across several valence and Rydberg excited states of small molecules, calculating the absorption spectra up to 10~eV. A plane-wave basis set is employed to accurately describe diffuse Rydberg excitations, while the transition dipole moment is evaluated from nonorthogonal Kohn--Sham determinants within the projector augmented wave formalism. Comparison with higher-level coupled-cluster results shows that orbital-optimized calculations provide a good description of oscillator strengths for states with predominantly single-configurational character, even with the generalized gradient approximation functional PBE. The inclusion of exact exchange and self-interaction correction further improves the results, with the latter yielding the smallest errors (mean absolute relative error of $\sim$25%). In contrast, large errors for all functionals are found for multi-configurational states, due to an inability of the approach to describe the multi-configurational character. Nonorthogonality between independently optimized states has previously been raised as a possible source of error in transition properties. In the present benchmark, no correlation of the nonorthogonality between the ground and excited states with the error on the transition intensity is found. These results establish the performance of orbital-optimized density functional calculations for absorption spectra of small molecules and highlight the need for extensions that combine state-specific orbital relaxation with a multi-configurational treatment.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Restaino, Diego Llorena Prieto, Jukka John, Yorick Leonard Adrian Schmerwitz, Elvar \"Orn J\'onsson, Gianluca Levi

item.title: Decoding Transient X-ray Absorption Spectra of Acetylacetone With Multireference Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Theory
item.description: arXiv:2608.09747v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Time-resolved X-ray absorption spectroscopy (TR-XAS) offers an element- and site-specific probe of coupled electronic and nuclear dynamics, but its interpretation requires methods that can treat multiconfigurational excited states across nonequilibrium nuclear ensembles. Here, we report time-resolved simulations of the acetylacetone (AcAc) transient X-ray absorption spectra by combining surface-hopping dynamics from complete active space second-order perturbation theory with multireference algebraic diagrammatic construction (MR-ADC). The simulated 20-200 fs spectra show a good agreement with experimental measurements and reveal that the TR-XAS response is governed by continuously evolving distributions of molecular geometries on the singlet potential energy surfaces (S2 and S1). In particular, absorption at 279.5-281.5 eV is enhanced for transient, nearly symmetric proton-sharing configurations, whereas the 284-286 eV profile reflects geometry-dependent C1s excitations modulated by proton transfer, bond alternation, and ring opening. For the long-time T_1 spectrum (7-10 ps), the principal features near 281.4 and 283.8 eV are assigned to central C 1s excitations into low-lying triplet pi-orbitals. Together, our simulations provide a more complete mechanistic picture of AcAc photorelaxation by directly linking ultrafast carbon K-edge signals to proton transfer, skeletal reorganization, internal conversion, and triplet formation.
item.dc:creator: Bennett W. Clark, Donna H. Odhiambo, Haden Dickerson, Alexander Yu. Sokolov

item.title: Low-rank approximation of Moment Tensor Potential enables reducing training set size without loss of accuracy
item.description: arXiv:2609.07372v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this study, we implement a low-rank approximation of Moment Tensor Potential (MTP) based on the tensor train (TT) decomposition. The implemented tensor-factorized MTP (TFMTP) and the original MTP model are actively trained via a MaxVol-based algorithm during molecular dynamics simulations of a four-component molten salt mixture, LiF-NaF-KF (FLiNaK), and geometry optimizations of a five-component equiatomic Mo-Nb-Ta-W-V random alloy. We demonstrate that under a 1.5-fold compression, TFMTP requires two times fewer configurations for fitting than the original MTP model, while maintaining an indistinguishable level of accuracy. These actively trained MTP and TFMTP models are further used to evaluate the density and viscosity of FLiNaK at temperatures ranging from 600 to 1200 K, as well as the elastic constants and bulk modulus of the Mo-Nb-Ta-W-V alloy at zero temperature. For both atomic systems, the differences in physical properties predicted by MTP and TFMTP are negligible.
item.dc:creator: Anna Bondarenko, Nikita Rybin, Maxim Rakhuba, Ivan S. Novikov

item.title: Tunable state-dependent interactions in collisionally stable mixtures of polar molecules
item.description: arXiv:2607.25777v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose encoding a pseudo-spin-$1/2$ system in the ground ($v=0$) and first excited ($v=1$) vibrational states of polar molecules. Double microwave shielding simultaneously shields molecules in both states, suppressing two-body losses by orders of magnitude while strictly avoiding three-body recombination. The microwave dressing is state-dependent and results in highly tunable, long-range dipolar Ising exchange ($J_z$), density-density ($V$), and spin-density ($W$) interactions. These interaction length scales readily exceed the typical interparticle spacing, pushing the molecules deep into the strongly interacting regime. In bulk gases, this enables the exploration of itinerant quantum magnetism and quantum droplets with novel anisotropic spin textures; in optical lattices, it naturally realizes extended Hubbard and $t$-$J_z$ models, opening new directions in quantum simulation.
item.dc:creator: Hubert J. J\'{o}\'{z}wiak, Hanwei Yang, Eugen Dizer, Arthur Christianen, Tijs Karman

item.title: Near-deterministic loading of molecular arrays by microwave-assisted collisions
item.description: arXiv:2607.25783v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Molecular tweezer arrays offer great prospects for quantum simulation, sensing, and computing, and would benefit from methods that enhance loading efficiency. Whereas light-assisted collisions underpin enhanced loading methods for atomic tweezer arrays, this approach cannot be directly extended to molecular arrays due to collisional loss. We show how this collisional loss can be suppressed by shelving molecules in rotationally or vibrationally excited states, so that a shelved molecule interacts with a newly loaded molecule through a repulsive van der Waals interaction. By introducing microwave assisted collisions, we show how to control the final states and the energy released in a collision between a pair of molecules. Following this controlled collision, one of the two molecules can be ejected, and we explore several strategies for ensuring deterministic ejection. Our schemes rely on currently available techniques for laser-coolable molecules, and we predict achievable filling fractions up to 96%, paving the way for scalable molecular arrays.
item.dc:creator: Etienne F. Walraven, Kang Feng, Jonas Rodewald, Michael R. Tarbutt, Tijs Karman

item.title: Response-state Learning for Transferable Vibrational Spectroscopic Characterization with Electron Prior
item.description: arXiv:2609.28935v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vibrational spectral prediction can become inaccurate when localized stereoelectronic environments perturb intermediate response states and high-risk response units dominate characteristic spectral fingerprints, making prediction across external chemical space difficult. SO(3) Equivariant Neural Kalman Networks (SENK) form a response-state cascade that combines an equivariant transformer backbone for Hessian, dipole-derivative and polarizability-derivative learning, an Equivariant Neural Kalman bridge for state-dependent refinement and reliability sensing, and an NBO-informed electronic-prior pathway coupling consistency regularization with bounded, branch-specific guided spectral calibration. SENK outperforms DetaNet on QM9S and QMe14S while preserving full-spectrum IR and Raman fidelity from small molecules to drug-like systems. SENK remains stable and selectively improves spectrally sensitive features in biomolecular systems with complex stereoelectronic effects. It therefore integrates tensor prediction, reliability diagnosis and physics-informed calibration, supporting transferable vibrational spectroscopy from molecular systems to functional molecular materials.
item.dc:creator: Zetong Li, Zhuosong Xie, Hengyu Fan, Jiaao Yu, Qiyao Hua, Zheng Lu, Liming Xu, Juanni Wu, Honglin Li
